players.product: regulated transmission & distribution utilities (ComEd, PECO, BGE, PHI) interconnecting data-center load in PJM

quarterly_data.signal: Exelon's Q2 2026 earnings presentation (Exhibit 99.2), slide 'Exelon's Projected Data Center Growth', splits projected data center growth into ~11 GW of High Probability Load (ComEd ~9 GW, MidAtlantic ~2 GW), described on the slide as 'Advanced phases of design or backed by FERC-approved TSAs (~40% with TSAs, backed by ~$1B in collateral)', and a ~25 GW Future Pipeline (ComEd ~17 GW, MidAtlantic ~8 GW) 'within current or future cluster studies (2026 and 2027 conclusion)'. The deck lists '$1B+ associated with committed high-density load projects' as the New Business category of its identified transmission opportunity, says its network serves 4 major cities including a top 5 data center market and a top 3 emerging data center market, and lists 'ComEd Announces New TSAs of 6.5+ GW' dated January 6, 2026.
quarterly_data.figure: high probability load ~11 GW (ComEd ~9 GW, MidAtlantic ~2 GW); future pipeline ~25 GW (ComEd ~17 GW, MidAtlantic ~8 GW); $1B+ transmission for committed high-density load projects; ComEd new TSAs 6.5+ GW

quarterly_data.signal: Exelon's consolidated statement of cash flows in the Q2 2026 earnings release (Exhibit 99.1) shows capital expenditures of $4,558 million for the six months ended June 30, 2026 versus $3,959 million a year earlier.
quarterly_data.figure: capex $4,558 million (six months ended June 30, 2026) vs $3,959 million
